channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: BoE’s Dhingra says financial conditions have already done much of the tightening
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) member Swati Dhingra struck a dovish tone on Thursday, highlighting signs of easing price pressures and weakness in the United Kingdom (UK) labour market, according to Reuters.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Downward momentum returns after 200-DMA break – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts, including Kenneth Broux, note that USD/MXN has broken above a multi-month descending trend line and reclaimed its 200-day moving average for the first time since April 2025.

item.title: PBoC vows to maintain loose monetary policy, keep Chinese Yuan stable
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBoC) said on Thursday that it will step up counter-cyclical adjustments and continue to implement an “appropriately loose” monetary policy, according to Reuters.

item.title: Euro: Downside risks start to shrink against US Dollar – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING argues EUR/USD’s break below 1.140 has pushed the pair into stretched undervaluation versus their short-term fair value model, as rate differentials moved in favour of the Euro.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $63.80 per troy ounce, down 0.98% from the $64.43 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher yields support currency – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes the US Dollar (USD) is strengthening as US fixed income sells off, driving global bond weakness and higher yields across the curve. A poor 5-year UST auction and strong US and global PMIs are reinforcing hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) rhetoric.

item.title: Euro jumps vs Swiss Franc after SNB decision, German IFO data supports
item.description: EUR/CHF gains 0.24% on Thursday and trades around 0.9415 at the time of writing, after reaching an intraday high of 0.9433 following the Swiss National Bank’s (SNB) monetary policy decision.

item.title: Indian Rupee declines significantly due to oil price recovery, surging US yields
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) extends its losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index gains ahead of weekly Initial Jobless Claims data
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is gaining ground for the fourth consecutive day and trading around 101.20 during European hours on Thursday.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Exchange rate seen weaker into year-end – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Mauricio Une and Renan Alves note that the Federal Reserve (Fed) raised rates by 25 bps and signaled a more restrictive stance, while Copom cut the Selic rate to 13.75%. The Brazilian Real (BRL) weakened slightly to BRL 5.1462 per USD but still outperformed most emerging peers.

item.title: Euro holds form against British Pound amid strong Eurozone data, hawkish BoE comments
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds gains against the British Pound (GBP) on Thursday, as the EUR/GBP flirts with the 0.8600 area, just below three-month highs, at 0.8607, following a 0.3% appreciation so far this week.

item.title: EUR/USD comes under pressure as Fed’s Williams warns of more interest rate hikes
item.description: The Euro (EUR) faces slight selling pressure against the US Dollar (USD), retreating from intraday high of around 1.1400 to near 1.1380 as the Greenback rises, following hawkish remarks from New York Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank John Willams, who is a permanent voting member.

item.title: Swiss Franc: SNB intervention bias dialed down – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note that EUR/CHF has rebounded about 0.3% after the Swiss National Bank (SNB) left rates at 0.0% but softened its FX intervention language.

item.title: Euro gains against Canadian Dollar on upbeat German IFO Business Index
item.description: EUR/CAD gains ground after registering modest losses the previous day, trading around 1.6060 during European hours on Thursday. The Euro (EUR) is appreciating as markets react positively to better-than-expected economic sentiment data out of Germany.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD plummets to near $63.60 after Fed Williams’ hawkish remarks
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down 1.25% to near $63.60 during the European trading session on Thursday. The white metal faces intense selling pressure after hawkish remarks from New York Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank John Willams, a permanent voting member, in the European trade.

item.title: South African Rand: SARB hikes again but environment stays tough – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur reports the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) raised its benchmark rate by 25 bps to 7.25%, the second hike this year as earlier expectations for cuts faded with higher Oil prices. Despite the move, South African Rand (ZAR) weakened, largely on Dollar strength.

item.title: Euro: Fiscal risks point lower against US Dollar - MUFG
item.description: Derek Halpenny at MUFG argues that widening French OAT/Bund spreads and global fixed income risk aversion are adding to negative momentum for the Euro. Political and fiscal uncertainties in France, including a large planned consolidation and budget risks, weigh on sentiment.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: Big challenge is on inflation
item.description: New York Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank John Willams said during the European trading session on Thursday that downside employment risks have eased and the economy is showing a strong demand from Artificial Intelligence (AI).

item.title: US Dollar: Rally starting to look stretched – ING
item.description: ING’s FX Strategist Francesco Pesole notes the Dollar has jumped, with DXY above 101.0, supported by strong US PMIs, higher Oil and soft risk sentiment, but now looks stretched versus fundamentals.

item.title: Swiss Franc dips to fresh four-month lows as SNB leaves interest rates at 0%
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) has given back previous gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, and fell to fresh four-month lows following the Swiss National Bank’s (SNB) monetary policy decision.

item.title: Swiss National Bank's Martin: Inflation likely to remain elevated for some time
item.description: Swiss National Bank (SNB) Vice Chairman Antoine Martin is addressing the press conference following the September monetary policy assessment, in which the central bank held interest rates unchanged at 0%.

item.title: Swiss National Bank's Tschudin: GDP growth exceptionally strong in Q2
item.description: Swiss National Bank governing board member Petra Tschudin said at the post-monetary policy assessment press conference on Thursday that the “Swiss GDP growth was exceptionally strong in Q2.”

item.title: Swiss National Bank's Schlegel: Will continue to monitor situation and adjust policy if necessary
item.description: Swiss National Bank (SNB) Chairman Martin Schlegel is speaking at the press conference after the June monetary policy assessment, explaining the reasons behind leaving the interest rate unchanged at 0%.

item.title: Dow Jones futures drop as Fed rate hike expectations surge
item.description: Dow Jones futures decline by 0.17% to trade near 51,780 during European hours on Thursday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures lose by 0.34% to trade around 7,750, while Nasdaq 100 futures depreciate 0.5% to trade near 30,610.

item.title: Gold struggles near one-week low as traders await Trump-Xi meeting amid Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) sticks to a negative bias for the second straight day, trading below the $4,300 mark or a one-week low during the first half of the European session as traders await a crucial meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA may follow hawkish market pricing – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur now expects the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to follow market pricing and deliver a rate hike next week, despite earlier assumptions of no further tightening.

item.title: Bank of England’s Lombardelli: Policy likely needed to tighten if energy risks persist
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli said on Thursday that “policy is increasingly likely to need to tighten if elevated energy prices persist, absent clear evidence of disinflation or weaker activity.”

item.title: Germany’s IFO Business Climate Index arrives higher at 89.9, beats 89.0 estimates
item.description: The German IFO Institute Business Climate Index improves at a faster-than-expected pace in September. The sentiment data arrives higher at 89.9 from estimates of 89.0 and 88.8 in August.

item.title: 0.7000: Key support zone for Australian Dollar ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) recovers a majority of its early losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. In early European session, the AUD/USD pair is marginally down to near 0.7035.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Volatility watch over autumn holidays – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Teppei Ino reviews recent USD/JPY price action, noting the pair opened near 153.41 before US Dollar (USD) buying ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and Bank of Japan (BoJ) meetings lifted it above 157.50.
